precepts.text: I am feeble and sore broken; I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart. Lord, all my desire is before thee. Some of you never pray for yourself because you think you are perfect. When you fast, ask Messiah to help you overcome your lust or your covetous spirit; we all have lust, though it differs.
precepts.point: Some of you will betray the brother next to you out of fear, because Esau threatens to tell the congregation what you were watching; your mind was in porn instead of the scriptures. With AI they will set many of us up with fake video, and some of our own people will believe it with no proof because they never built their minds in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
David was down but not out, and he did not hide it from God: “I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.” To roar is to utter or express in a loud tone: to cry, shout, yell. David says, I'm feeble, I'm broken, and I cried out because of the disquietness of my heart.

“Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.” He laid it all before the Lord.

Some of you, when you pray, do not pray for yourself, because you think you are perfect. You need to pray for yourself and ask for help to overcome certain things. Some of you are fighting lust; when you fast, pray that Messiah helps you overcome that lust. We all have lust. Our lust might be different things, but we all have it. Some of you are fighting a covetous spirit; pray that Messiah helps you overcome it.

You are not going to walk into the kingdom of heaven thinking you're perfect and your stuff don't stink. Put your desire and your groaning before the Lord, so that when the storm comes, fear does not overtake you.

precepts.text: David felt his own iniquities as a burden too heavy and leaned on the Lord — show me where I am wrong. A lot of you take correction and then pray the Lord judge the man who corrected you.
precepts.point: Wisdom came as a gift and became a trial: the same man wrote that increasing knowledge increases sorrow. It can crush you or make you rise.

precepts.text: His lovers and friends stood aloof from his sore, his kinsmen stood afar off, and those who sought his life laid snares and spoke mischievous things; but he was as a deaf and dumb man who opened not his mouth, having no room to speak for what he did.
precepts.point: David asks the Lord to make haste to help him and to put to shame those who seek after his soul to destroy it, and those who say "Aha" to mock him for his transgressions.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it”. Psalm 38 shows who they were: “My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my sore; and my kinsmen stand afar off. They also that seek after my life lay snares for me: and they that seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and imagine deceits all the day long.” His own lovers and friends stood aloof, his kinsmen stood afar off, and those who sought his life laid snares and spoke mischievous things.

And David could say nothing back. He was as a deaf and dumb man who opened not his mouth, because he had no room to speak for what he did. The ones who said to him “Aha, aha” were mocking him for his transgressions, so he does not answer them himself; he asks the Lord to “make haste to help me” and to drive them backward and put them to shame.

points: This is a chapter where David was going through some things. He asks the Most High not to rebuke him in wrath nor chasten him in hot displeasure, for the arrows stick fast in him and the hand presses him sore.
There is no soundness in his flesh because of the anger, no rest in his bones because of his sin; his iniquities are gone over his head as a heavy burden.
His wounds stink and are corrupt because of his foolishness; he is troubled, bowed down greatly, and goes mourning all day long, for his loins are filled with a loathsome disease.
Given the loins filled with a loathsome disease and the wounds that stink and are corrupt, David had an ancient sexually transmitted disease. It may seem like he did not, but keep reading.
David is feeble and sore broken and has roared by reason of the disquietness of his heart; all his desire is before the Most High and his groaning is not hid.

His heart pants, his strength fails, and the light of his eyes is gone from him. His lovers and friends stand aloof from his sore and his kinsmen stand afar off. If the trouble is in his loins and even his kinsmen stand afar off from his sore, that tells you what it is. A lot of brothers and sisters need to read this; there is nothing new under the sun.

They that seek after his life lay snares and speak mischievous things and imagine deceit all day long. When you get plagued like that and catch diseases because of foolish things you do, people start talking about you.

But David was as a deaf man that heard not and a dumb man that opened not his mouth, in whose mouth are no reproofs. He could not even say anything back; everybody was talking bad about him but what could he say.
Here David starts to repent. For in the Most High does he hope; he asks to be heard lest his enemies rejoice over him when his foot slips.
David is ready to halt and his sorrow is continually before him; he declares his iniquity and is sorry for his sin. That is David showing godly sorrow.
His enemies are lively and strong, and they that hate him wrongfully are multiplied; they render evil for good and are his adversaries because he follows the thing that good is.
He asks the Most High not to forsake him nor be far off, but to make haste to help him, his salvation. Though David caught some disease, he still showed godly sorrow and repentance.
